defs: go and look to see if it is okay
look at something to learn how it is
go see if someone is all right
exs: I will check on the cat now.
Please check your bag before you leave.
Mom went to check on the baby.

defs: go up or into with hands and feet
move up using your hands and legs
move up to a higher place using your hands and feet
exs: The cat can climb up the tree.
I climb into bed at nine.
Kids climb the wall at the park.

defs: breathe in fast because you are surprised
make a quick sound when you are shocked
take a sudden breath in surprise
exs: We gasp when the lights go out.
Mom will gasp if she sees the mess.
The kids gasp at the big magic trick.

defs: was resting with the body flat on
rested flat on top of something
had the body flat on a place
exs: The dog lay on the sofa all day.
I lay on the grass and looked up.
She lay on her bed and read a book.

defs: make a long, sad sound
say something in an unhappy voice
complain with a low, sad sound
exs: Dad will moan when he sees the mess.
I moan when I have too much homework.
The sick boy began to moan in bed.

defs: made an angry face
looked at someone in an unhappy way
frowned because of feeling angry
exs: Dad scowled when the milk fell down.
The girl scowled at her broken toy.
My brother scowled when I took his seat.

defs: the highest part of something
the upper end of a thing
the place that is farthest up
exs: Do not fill the cup to the top.
The cat sat on the top of the box.
We ran to the top of the hill.

defs: not having something with you
not doing something at that time
with no one or nothing present
exs: I cannot go to school without my bag.
Dad made breakfast without any help.
Do not cross the road without looking.

defs: one thing after another in a set way
the way things are placed one by one
the right way to put things in a line
exs: Put the numbers in order, one to ten.
The kids stood in order from short to tall.
Read the pages in order, not just any page.

defs: a small bag for carrying things
a little sack on the body
a soft bag where a baby animal stays
exs: The baby kangaroo sleeps in its pouch.
I keep my pencils in a small pouch.
She put her coins in a leather pouch.

defs: laugh or shout very loudly
make a very loud sound
make a big, loud noise
exs: The kids roar with laughter at the joke.
The lion will roar at the zoo.
The class began to roar when the clown fell.

defs: telling or giving to others in a group
using something together with other people
time to show or tell things to the class
exs: Sharing time is my favorite part of class.
Sharing toys with friends is kind.
We have sharing time on Friday morning.

defs: the sound you make when you speak
the sound that comes from your mouth
what you hear when someone talks
exs: I heard Dad's voice in the kitchen.
Her voice is soft and sweet.
Please use your quiet voice in the library.

defs: in a quiet way without being upset
slowly and quietly, not angry
without showing worry or anger
exs: Mom spoke calmly when the dog ran away.
He calmly sat down and waited.
The teacher calmly asked us to line up.

defs: the leader of a team or ship
the person in charge of a group
the boss of a ship or plane
exs: The captain of our team is Tom.
The captain drove the ship to the port.
Who will be the captain in the school play?

defs: sad because things did not go as you hoped
unhappy because you did not get what you wanted
a little sad about a bad result
exs: I was disappointed when it rained on picnic day.
Mia felt disappointed about her test score.
He looked disappointed when the game ended early.

defs: a little afraid before something new
worried and not calm
feeling a bit scared inside
exs: I feel nervous before the big test.
She was nervous on the first day of school.
The boy is nervous about singing on stage.

defs: a person with an important job on a ship
a helper who is second to the leader
a person who has a high job in a team
exs: The officer helped the captain drive the ship.
My uncle is an officer on a big ship.
The first officer gave the ship's report.

defs: the role an actor plays in a show
the person an actor acts as in a play
the job you do in a school play
exs: I want the part of the king in the play.
She got the part of the little duck.
Which part do you want in our class play?

defs: say that you will surely do something
tell someone you will really do it
give your word to do something
exs: I promise to clean my room today.
Dad will promise to take us to the zoo.
Do you promise to be home by six?

defs: the break time between school classes
time to play outside at school
free time during the school day
exs: We play ball at recess every day.
The bell rings and recess begins.
I ate a snack with Amy at recess.

defs: said something in a quick, angry way
spoke to someone in a rude, angry voice
talked in a short and mean way
exs: Tom snapped at his sister, "Go away!"
Dad was tired and snapped at us.
"Be quiet!" the girl snapped at the dog.
